title: AFRICAN GOLD
author: Andries J. Greyling
rationale: South African adventure novel (KwaZulu-Natal, Witwatersrand, Mpumalanga). isiZulu is the primary regional language (KZN/Zulu setting). Afrikaans applies for SA/Namibia rule. Spanish + French are catalog-wide market languages.

targets.name: isiZulu
directives: Voice: everyday isiZulu as spoken in KwaZulu-Natal (Durban, Pietermaritzburg, rural KZN) — warm, direct, alive. NOT formal SABC/broadcast register, NOT academic-paper Zulu, NOT the stiff isiZulu of government documents or textbooks.

Do NOT invent pseudo-Zulu transliterations of English words (e.g. ithri-loji for 'trilogy', i-derrick for 'derrick', i-handset for 'handset'). Either use the established Zulu word, or leave the English term as a natural code-switch exactly as a KZN speaker would — without prefixing every English noun with i-.
Translate into standard isiZulu as written in KwaZulu-Natal, with respectful registers (sawubona/sanibona, isiHlonipho where scenes call for it).

South African English words the source code-switches into — bakkie, biltong, stoep, veld, kopje, donga, drift, highveld, rooibos — may stay as code-switches where a natural isiZulu speaker would use the English or Afrikaans form; do not invent neologisms for mining / engineering equipment.
Proper names, invented entities (the Court, SAGE), and place names stay verbatim.
Technical / mining / geological terms (stope, reef, shaft, grade, carat, diff) may stay in English where that is natural in KZN technical speech.
Do NOT translate or paraphrase any isiZulu phrases already present in the source — they are home language and read naturally to the target reader.

targets.name: Afrikaans
directives: Voice: the people's Afrikaans — contemporary, lived-in, how South Africans actually speak at the braai, on the mine, in the bakkie. NOT Hoog-Afrikaans, NOT Netherlands Dutch, NOT archaic Bybel-Afrikaans, NOT newsreader or sermon register.

Dialogue and informal narration should use natural spoken rhythm: contractions where English has them, direct address, idiomatic turns. Avoid textbook phrases (ten opsigte van, dit is van die grootste belang, derhalwe) unless a character is deliberately formal.
Natural, contemporary South African Afrikaans (Standaardafrikaans with lived warmth), not Netherlands Dutch and not archaic Bybel-Afrikaans.

South African English words the source uses (bakkie, donga, kopje, drift, highveld, rooibos, biltong, stoep, veld) are also natural Afrikaans words — keep them verbatim where they are already in the source.
isiZulu phrases that appear in the source stay verbatim and untranslated into Afrikaans — they read as isiZulu to an Afrikaans reader exactly as they do to an English one.
Mining / geological / engineering terms may stay in English where an Afrikaans speaker would naturally code-switch.
Invented entities (the Court, SAGE, Brotherhood) and proper names stay verbatim.

targets.name: Spanish
directives: Neutral/international Spanish (español neutro) for the widest readership.

ALL South African words — isiZulu terms AND cultural flavour words (bakkie, biltong, stoep, veld, kopje, donga, drift, highveld, rooibos, biltong) — stay verbatim and italicised as foreign terms. Do not Hispanicise them and do not add footnotes the source lacks.
Invented entities (the Court, SAGE, Brotherhood) keep their English names.
Preserve the code-switching texture: the foreignness is the point.

targets.name: French
directives: Standard international French.
Same foreign-term rule as Spanish: South African words (bakkie, biltong, stoep, veld, kopje, donga, drift, highveld, rooibos) stay verbatim, italicised, unglossed.
Invented entities (the Court, SAGE, Brotherhood) keep their English names.
Respect register shifts: the mine floor and the clandestine meetings are different Frenches.

global_directives: REGISTER: These are novels for real readers, not textbooks or news broadcasts. Regional editions (Afrikaans, isiZulu) must sound like people actually talk — stoep, mine floor, taxi rank — not bulletin or sermon register.

PRESERVE the front-matter structure of build/BOOK.md exactly: title block, copyright page, dedication, epigraphs, chapter order, and any back matter. Translate their CONTENT; keep their ORDER and markdown structure byte-for-byte where structural (headings, '---' rules, '⁂' breaks).
The copyright notice, ISBN line, and 'Published by the House of Greyling' stay — translate surrounding prose but keep proper nouns and legal sense intact.
Do NOT add translator's notes, footnotes, or bracketed glosses the English source does not contain.
Chapter titles ARE translated unless they are proper nouns.
Output one file per language at build/BOOK.<code>.md, ready for tools/render_book.sh.
